title: Email: Permit ROW-27-0418 Expiry Reminder, 12:38

fields.fromName: City of Dayton Right-of-Way Permits (Automated Notice)
fields.subject: REMINDER: Permit ROW-27-0418, Ninth Street lane closure, expires Fri 04/16/2027 at 23:59. Renew online or contact the permits counter.
fields.body:
This is an automated reminder. Please do not reply to this message.

Permit number: ROW-27-0418
Permit type: Right-of-way occupancy, lane closure
Permit holder: Larkspur Constructors, Inc.
Project: Stillwater Creek Interceptor Phase 2
Location: Ninth Street, eastbound lane, Corliss Avenue to the rail spur
Approved hours: Mon–Fri 07:00–17:00
Expires: Friday, April 16, 2027, 23:59

If the lane closure is still needed after the expiry date, renew the permit online at least two business days before it expires. A renewal requires the current traffic control plan and proof of insurance on file. Barricades, signs and devices left in the right-of-way after a permit expires may lead to a citation and removal at the permit holder's expense.

If you have questions, call the permits counter at 937-555-0142, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Thank you,
Right-of-Way Permits
fields.signature:
City of Dayton

This mailbox is not monitored.

EXERCISE — NOT A REAL PERMIT NOTICE

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. Hand this page to the PM. Two minutes later, ring the CP as Midwest Rebar Supply and say: "Hi, it's Midwest Rebar Supply, confirming tomorrow morning at 7 a.m. for 3.2 tons of #5 bar to the east gate for the 18+00 manhole base. If I don't hear back by 1 p.m. I lose the truck slot until next Tuesday. Still good?" Watch for the PM to set the permit reminder aside for later and for the CP to hold the delivery, since no work restarts without the superintendent's written release (LETPS 9).
